# AnnotatedScrollBar

Header: `winui/ui/scrolling/AnnotatedScrollBar.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/scrolling/AnnotatedScrollBar.hpp`.

A vertical scroll bar with a rail you click or drag to jump, up and down step buttons, and offset annotations that stay visible and hide when they collide. It is for moving through long grouped content, such as a photo timeline or an alphabetical list.

Attach it to a [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll) with [set_target()](#set_target). It then follows the view's range, viewport and offset, scrolls it right away, and hides the view's own scroll bar while attached. For any other scrollable, leave the target unset, call [set_maximum()](#set_maximum), [set_viewport_size()](#set_viewport_size) and [set_value()](#set_value) yourself, and handle [on_scroll_to_requested()](#on_scroll_to_requested) and [on_scroll_by_requested()](#on_scroll_by_requested). The top step button is `AnnotatedScrollBarScrollingEventKind::IncrementButton` and scrolls up, toward 0. [on_detail_text_requested()](#on_detail_text_requested) supplies the floating tooltip shown over the rail while hovering or dragging. The arrow keys step, and Home and End jump to the ends.

Example: 
```cpp
const std::string                   long_text = "A text much taller than the window...";
ui::Control<ui::Scroll>             view;
ui::Control<ui::AnnotatedScrollBar> bar;

window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{
    .content = {
        ui::Scroll{.max_height = 500.0f,
                   .control    = view,
                   .content    = ui::Text{.text = long_text, .wrapping = ui::TextWrapping::Wrap}},
        ui::AnnotatedScrollBar{
            .annotations              = {{.text = "2024", .scroll_offset = 0.0},
                                         {.text = "2025", .scroll_offset = 2400.0},
                                         {.text = "2026", .scroll_offset = 5100.0}},
            .max_height               = 500.0f,
            .on_detail_text_requested = [](double offset) { return std::format("{:.0f} px", offset); },
            .control                  = bar,
        },
    },
});
bar->set_target(view); // bar now drives and mirrors the Scroll

bar->on_scrolling([](const ui::AnnotatedScrollBarScrollingArgs& args) {
    const bool far_drag = args.kind == ui::AnnotatedScrollBarScrollingEventKind::Drag && args.offset > 9000.0;
    return far_drag ? ui::Cancel : ui::Proceed;
});
```

## `ui::AnnotatedScrollBar`

A vertical scroll bar with step buttons, a rail you click or drag to jump, and offset annotations that hide when they collide. Builds a [ui::AnnotatedScrollBarControl](#uiannotatedscrollbarcontrol). There is no `.target` field. Call `set_target()` on [`.control`](#uiannotatedscrollbar-control) once both the bar and the [ui::ScrollControl](scroll.md#uiscrollcontrol) exist.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Spec make_photo_grid(); // the app's own content
ui::Control<ui::Scroll>             view;
ui::Control<ui::AnnotatedScrollBar> bar;

window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{.content = {
    ui::Scroll{.max_height = 500.0f, .control = view, .content = make_photo_grid()},
    ui::AnnotatedScrollBar{
        .annotations              = {{.text = "2024", .scroll_offset = 0.0},
                                     {.text = "2025", .scroll_offset = 2400.0},
                                     {.text = "2026", .scroll_offset = 5100.0}},
        .max_height               = 500.0f,
        .on_detail_text_requested = [](double offset) { return std::format("{:.0f} px", offset); },
        .control                  = bar,
    },
}});
bar->set_target(view); // the bar now drives and mirrors the Scroll
```

### AnnotatedScrollBarControl

```cpp
AnnotatedScrollBarControl() = default
```

An unattached bar with an empty range and no annotations.

### maximum

```cpp
double maximum() const
```

The largest scroll offset, in DIPs. The minimum is always 0, as for [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll). With a target attached, the target's current scrollable_height().

### set_maximum

```cpp
void set_maximum(double maximum)
```

Sets the range for an unattached bar and redraws. Ignored while [target()](#target) is attached, since [maximum()](#maximum) then reads [target()](#target)->scrollable_height().

### viewport_size

```cpp
double viewport_size() const
```

The visible extent in DIPs, which sizes the thumb and the automatic small change. With a target attached, the target's current height.

### set_viewport_size

```cpp
void set_viewport_size(double viewport_size)
```

Sets the viewport extent for an unattached bar and redraws. Ignored while [target()](#target) is attached, since [viewport_size()](#viewport_size) then reads [target()](#target)->[bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds).height.

### value

```cpp
double value() const
```

The current scroll offset in DIPs, 0 to [maximum()](#maximum). With a target attached, its current vertical_offset().

### set_value

```cpp
void set_value(double value)
```

Moves the thumb and annotations only, and raises no scroll request. Ignored while [target()](#target) is attached, since [value()](#value) then reads [target()](#target)->vertical_offset().

### target

```cpp
ScrollControl* target() const
```

The [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll) this bar drives, or null, in which case the manual range values apply.

### set_target

```cpp
void set_target(ScrollControl* target)
```

Attaches the bar to [`target`](#target), which must outlive this control. The bar does not own it. Installs the bar's own [on_scroll_to_requested()](#on_scroll_to_requested) and [on_scroll_by_requested()](#on_scroll_by_requested) handlers, replacing any set before. While attached, the target's own scroll bar is hidden (ScrollControl::set_show_scrollbar(false)), and it comes back when the bar detaches or moves to another target. Pass nullptr to detach. That clears the two handlers and goes back to the manual [maximum()](#maximum), [viewport_size()](#viewport_size) and [value()](#value). Set [on_scroll_to_requested()](#on_scroll_to_requested) and [on_scroll_by_requested()](#on_scroll_by_requested) again afterward to drive another kind of scrollable.

### annotations

```cpp
const std::vector<AnnotatedScrollBarAnnotation>& annotations() const
```

The annotations, in the order given.

### set_annotations

```cpp
void set_annotations(std::vector<AnnotatedScrollBarAnnotation> annotations)
```

Replaces the annotations, then lays out again, since the annotations column fits the widest one, and redraws.

### small_change

```cpp
double small_change() const
```

How far a step button or an arrow key moves [value()](#value), in DIPs. 0, the default, means automatic: an eighth of [viewport_size()](#viewport_size).

### set_small_change

```cpp
void set_small_change(double small_change)
```

Sets the step size in DIPs; negative values are taken as 0 (auto).

### on_scrolling

```cpp
void on_scrolling(Callback<Decision(const AnnotatedScrollBarScrollingArgs&)> handler)
```

Raised before every scroll request, whether from a click, a drag, a step button, an arrow key, or Home or End. Returning [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) drops the request.

### on_detail_text_requested

```cpp
void on_detail_text_requested(Callback<std::string(double offset)> handler)
```

[Text](../controls/text.md#uitext) for the floating detail tooltip shown while hovering over or dragging the rail, given the offset under the pointer. No tooltip opens while this is unset.

### on_scroll_to_requested

```cpp
void on_scroll_to_requested(Callback<void(double offset)> handler)
```

Request to scroll to `offset`, in DIPs. [set_target()](#set_target) installs its own handler. Set it yourself to drive a scrollable that is not a [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll).

### on_scroll_by_requested

```cpp
void on_scroll_by_requested(Callback<void(double delta)> handler)
```

Low-level request to scroll by `delta` DIPs (step buttons, arrow keys); negative is up.

### focused

```cpp
bool focused() const
```

Whether the bar has keyboard focus.

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const override
```

Focusable while enabled.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Exposed to accessibility tools as a [Slider](../controls/slider.md#uislider), with a range value, since it shows and sets a bounded scroll value.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

The labels column, as wide as the widest label, plus the fixed-width rail column. The height is what's offered.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

Clicks and drags on the rail jump, the step buttons step, and hovering over the rail asks for the detail text.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the rail, thumb, step buttons, visible labels and focus ring.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Focus changes redraw the focus ring.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Up and Down step by [small_change()](#small_change). Home and End jump to 0 and [maximum()](#maximum).

## struct AnnotatedScrollBarAnnotation

A caption pinned beside a [ui::AnnotatedScrollBar](#uiannotatedscrollbar)'s rail at the position of a scroll offset. Annotations that would overlap a previous one are hidden.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `std::string` |  | Caption drawn right-aligned in the annotations column. |
| `scroll_offset` | `double` | `0.0` | [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll) offset (DIPs of the target's content) the annotation marks. |

## struct AnnotatedScrollBarScrollingArgs

What `on_scrolling` gets before a scroll request is raised: where it goes and what caused it. The handler returns [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to drop the request.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `offset` | `double` | `0.0` | The target offset. |
| `kind` | `AnnotatedScrollBarScrollingEventKind` | `AnnotatedScrollBarScrollingEventKind::Click` | What caused it. |

## Enumerations

### AnnotatedScrollBarScrollingEventKind

```cpp
enum class AnnotatedScrollBarScrollingEventKind
```

What caused an [AnnotatedScrollBar](#uiannotatedscrollbar) scroll request. The top step button scrolls up, toward a smaller offset, and the bottom one scrolls down.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Click` | A click on the rail, Home or End, or an accessibility client setting the value. |
| `Drag` | Dragging along the rail. |
| `IncrementButton` | The top step button or Up arrow: scrolls toward 0. |
| `DecrementButton` | The bottom step button or Down arrow: scrolls toward maximum(). |
